item.title: Lamar dominates second half to end Houston Christian's winning streak
item.description: Lamar took control of a close game in the second half to deny Houston Christian its third consecutive win. (Michael Wade/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) BEAUMONT - Houston Christian's bid for a third consecutive win was denied as Lamar rolled to a 35-10 win Saturday at Provost Umphrey Stadium. Lamar (6-2, 4-1 Southland) scored the game's final 21 points to pull away from HCU (4-4, 3-2). Javon Bejarano's 55-yard interception return for a touchdown in the final minute of the first half drew the Huskies within 14-10 at halftime. But Lamar dominated after the break, getting a 6-yard TD run from Jojo Uga and a 41-yard scoring pass from Aiden McCown to Davin Driskell in the third quarter. The Cardinals tacked on Cam Patterson's 15-yard TD run early in the fourth quarter for the final margin. HCU stays on the road next week with a Saturday game at Stephen F. Austin. item.title: 🎥 Evander breaks goalscoring duck with MLS Goal of the Week entry 💣
item.description: 🎥 Evander breaks goalscoring duck with MLS Goal of the Week entry 💣 FC Cincinnati have been below their usual standards compared to recent seasons across the ongoing 2026 MLS campaign, with the Orange and Blue facing a late fight to reach the playoffs. An away day at Audi Field against foundering DC United came at the right time for Pat Noonan's outfit, with Evander looking to put an end to his difficult drought in front of goal. The Brazilian would deliver a masterclass in long-range finishing to do just that. One of the league's best-ever from outside of the box, the 28-year-old midfielder unleashed a dipping, unstoppable hit in the 35th minute to break the deadlock against the Black-and-Red in a way perhaps only he knows how. It was Evander's first goal since August 22nd at home against Seattle, snapping a seven-match goalless run for a player who has, once again, been in the conversation for league MVP on the back of being one of just eight players in double figures in both goals (14) and assists (14). Cincinnati may be a shadow of themselves this term, but any possible playoff run (should they qualify) will undoubtedly hinge on more Evander heroics. An entry for Goal of the Week certainly will not hurt, either.

item.title: Sports media world reacts to chaotic ending of UCF’s upset over BYU
item.description: Credit: Fox Moments after his team pulled off the most significant win in program history, UCF Knights head coach Scott Frost spoke for everyone. “That’s the weirdest end of a game I’ve ever seen,” Frost said to Fox sideline reporter Alexa Landestoy , while surrounded by a sea of black and gold. UCF (4-3) upset the No. 2 BYU Cougars (6-1), 39-31 in double overtime, to secure the first win against a top-five-ranked opponent in school history. The result itself was wild enough, but the path to victory was a brand of mayhem unique to college football. Coach Scott Frost could not be happier with his team and the way things finished as they pulled off the crazy upset against BYU @alexalandestoy https://t.co/ZFI9uJ4RP6 — FOX College Football (@CFBONFOX) October 24, 2026 With just under two minutes left in regulation and the game tied at 24, the BYU defense stuffed UCF quarterback Keyone Jenkins on fourth-and-goal. Would you have kicked here? https://t.co/2Ly0CKy2jU — Tom Fornelli (@TomFornelli) October 24, 2026 The BYU offense rewarded the defense by going three-and-out, and that’s when the madness truly began. Overtime looked inevitable until BYU defensive tackle Keanu Tanuvasa committed an unsportsmanlike conduct penalty, setting UCF up in field goal range. Instead of kicking right away, with 14 seconds left, Frost sent his offense back out there. Jenkins inexplicably spiked the ball before throwing an incompletion, and then Will Stone missed a 46-yard field goal attempt. Still, the game didn’t head directly into overtime. Stone’s kick was blocked, and he recovered the ball with two seconds on the clock, seemingly allowing UCF a redo at the game winner. But because BYU ripped Stone’s helmet off during the recovery, we got a 10-second runoff, which Terry McAulay disagreed with , and then the game entered overtime. A circus show finish to regulation sends the BYU-UCF game to OT. Connor Onion, Robert Griffin III, and rules analyst Mike Pereira provide the commentary for Fox. https://t.co/8u2Jb0vd1P — Awful Announcing (@awfulannouncing) October 24, 2026 In overtime, BYU quarterback Bear Bachmeier threw a 28-yard touchdown, and Jenkins responded with a 25-yard touchdown pass to Josh Derry to even the score at 31—and prompt Robert Griffin III to call BYU’s defense “lactose intolerant” from his Fox booth with Connor Onion. In double overtime, BYU seemingly forced UCF to settle for a field goal. But BYU’s Kendal Wall earned a roughing-the-kicker penalty, and Jenkins made them pay with a touchdown pass and successful two-point conversion. BYU failed to answer on the ensuing possession, granting UCF a chaotic, well-earned upset. item.title: Where Did Ferrari Lose Pace in F1 US GP Qualifying? Hamilton and Leclerc Answer
item.description: Lewis Hamilton and Charles Leclerc lamented conditions and ttiresafter a disappointing end to F1 US GP qualifying. After topping the three F1 practice sessions shared between Hamilton and Leclerc, it all came undone in qualifying for the US GP at the Circuit of the Americas. They ended up only fourth and fifth after a bad start in Q3 on the first run. They both managed to improve in the second run, but it was a marginal gain. In the end, Leclerc was fourth and Hamilton fifth, when Mercedes’ Andrea Kimi Antonelli took pole from the Red Bull pair of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. Both Antonelli and Hadjar managed to get ahead of them from where they were in practice. It is a story of how Ferrari has been all year long in F1 qualifying. The conditions changed a bit by the end of qualifying, which affected their run. For Hamilton , he felt pretty solid with the tyre preparation and the lap; he had no issues. But he lamented the lack of straight-line speed, which he feels is the limiting factor for Ferrari. He reiterated that their F1 rivals have caught up on the cornering speed, but they have not gained as much on the engine side. Hamilton Had No Issues As Straight-Line Speed Comes in Picture “I don’t know; I haven’t looked at the data,” said Hamilton to the media after US GP qualifying. “We know that throughout the weekend we look at the straight, like just up to Turn 1, Max; when we cut power, they just keep pulling. “And that’s similar in another place, like into Turn 11, where I think it might be similar, maybe into Turn 12, but then the rest of the lap a little bit; you see it on the overlay, but I don’t know what happened; the car felt really good. The lap was solid, so they were just. “I had a really good out lap. It’s a clean lap, no issues at all really. I think that’s the only place where I think our car is really solid. At least as good as this, maybe slightly better than maybe the other, but I think they have closed up on the chassis. We’ve seen Red Bull close up on their downforce. “Mercedes took a good three-tenths step of lap time at least they saw a couple of races ago. I think they’re starting to figure out how to utilise that, and so they’re now matching us, but we’re not able to take that step to close that speed on the straight,” summed up Hamilton, who notes that the gap varies from race to race. After topping the three F1 practice sessions shared between Hamilton and Leclerc, it all came undone in qualifying for the US GP at the Circuit of the Americas. They ended up only fourth and fifth after a bad start in Q3 on the first run. They both managed to improve in the second run, but it was a marginal gain. In the end, Leclerc was fourth and Hamilton fifth, when Mercedes’ Andrea Kimi Antonelli took pole from the Red Bull pair of Max Verstappen and Isack Hadjar. Both Antonelli and Hadjar managed to get ahead of them from where they were in practice. It is a story of how Ferrari has been all year long in F1 qualifying. The conditions changed a bit by the end of qualifying, which affected their run. For Hamilton , he felt pretty solid with the tyre preparation and the lap; he had no issues. But he lamented the lack of straight-line speed, which he feels is the limiting factor for Ferrari. He reiterated that their F1 rivals have caught up on the cornering speed, but they have not gained as much on the engine side. Hamilton Had No Issues As Straight-Line Speed Comes in Picture “I don’t know; I haven’t looked at the data,” said Hamilton to the media after US GP qualifying. “We know that throughout the weekend we look at the straight, like just up to Turn 1, Max; when we cut power, they just keep pulling. “And that’s similar in another place, like into Turn 11, where I think it might be similar, maybe into Turn 12, but then the rest of the lap a little bit; you see it on the overlay, but I don’t know what happened; the car felt really good. The lap was solid, so they were just. “I had a really good out lap. It’s a clean lap, no issues at all really. I think that’s the only place where I think our car is really solid. At least as good as this, maybe slightly better than maybe the other, but I think they have closed up on the chassis. We’ve seen Red Bull close up on their downforce. “Mercedes took a good three-tenths step of lap time at least they saw a couple of races ago. I think they’re starting to figure out how to utilise that, and so they’re now matching us, but we’re not able to take that step to close that speed on the straight,” summed up Hamilton, who notes that the gap varies from race to race. It’s a bit easier for them to extract the lap time in Q3 than it is for us, and as soon as we are a tiny bit outside the window, we pay a lot the price. So, this is something that we need to look into,” summed up Leclerc, who was expecting a step up from Q2 to Q3 which never came for him. item.title: Charles Leclerc sets boundaries with Lewis Hamilton ahead of Turn 1 battle
item.description: Motorsport photo Charles Leclerc and Lewis Hamilton will start Sunday's United States Grand Prix fourth and fifth on the grid, but the Monegasque says both drivers know "the line not to cross" heading into Turn 1 of the Austin circuit. Leclerc qualified ahead of his team-mate but has admitted that both he and Hamilton have overstepped at times throughout the season. One example of this came at Monza earlier this year. The pair made contact on the opening lap of Ferrari's home race as Hamilton lunged up the inside of Turn 1. Leclerc kept his line into Turn 2, pushing his team-mate off the track. Hamilton dropped from fourth to tenth and later recovered to sixth, while Leclerc crashed out of the race on just the second lap. Hamilton was critical at the time, saying: “Here, there are no rules. We need to address that.” Leclerc added, “Here, it’s true though that we went too far. I think Lewis in Turn 1, then Turn 2, I tried to do the tightest corner possible, but that was just not enough - and doing it here is not good." Charles Leclerc, Ferrari Charles Leclerc, Ferrari With both Ferraris starting close together on the first run up the hill to Turn 1 at COTA, Leclerc assured fans that neither of them will be making any aggressive manoeuvres on the other. Asked whether the team had put any rules in place for the initial lunge, Leclerc was clear on what was expected from them both. “No, we know what is the line not to cross, and again I think we’ve got some occasions throughout the year where I’ve crossed it, Lewis crossed it and we don’t want to see that." Teamwork will be an important part of the grand prix for the Scuderia pair. “I mean it’s always important. I don’t think on a track like this there’s anything like Singapore like that you can do with slowing down and all the team or whatsoever, but obviously just stay away from each other is always a good thing no matter where we are.” To read more Motorsport.com articles visit our website .

item.description: NEW ORLEANS, LOUISIANA - OCTOBER 11: Head coach Kellen Moore of the New Orleans Saints looks on against the Minnesota Vikings during the second half at Caesars Superdome on October 11, 2026 in New Orleans, Louisiana. (Photo by Chris Graythen/Getty Images) Getty The New Orleans Saints picked up a much-needed victory over the New York Giants in Week 6. Nearly a week later, three of their defensive players are paying for what happened during the game. The NFL fined defensive end Chase Young, defensive tackle Christen Miller and defensive tackle Vernon Broughton a combined $35,222 for separate violations during New Orleans’ 34-27 victory on October 18. According to the league’s official accountability report, released Saturday, October 24, Young received the largest punishment, a $14,926 fine for unsportsmanlike conduct involving a violent gesture. Miller was fined $11,915 for the same violation, while Broughton received an $8,381 fine for a hit on a quarterback involving contact to the head or neck. Interestingly, the NFL listed Young’s and Miller’s violations at exactly the same point in the third quarter. Chase Young, Christen Miller Fined for Violent Gestures Against Giants Young and Miller were both penalized financially for actions occurring with 39 seconds remaining in the third quarter of the Saints’ victory. The NFL classified both violations as unsportsmanlike conduct, specifically citing a “violent gesture.” The identical timestamps suggest the fines stemmed from the same sequence, although the league’s published report does not describe the gestures or establish whether the players were celebrating together. Young’s $14,926 fine was $3,011 higher than the amount assessed to Miller. Both players contributed to a strong defensive performance as New Orleans snapped a three-game losing streak. Young recorded 1.5 sacks against the Giants, matching Carl Granderson for the team lead. The Saints finished with five sacks and four takeaways, including three interceptions. New Orleans needed those defensive contributions after watching a 34-10 advantage shrink to seven points during the fourth quarter. The Saints ultimately held on, securing their second victory of the season and improving to 2-4. McCarthy entered in the second half. The NFL’s fine report does not identify the quarterback involved in Broughton’s violation. Unlike the fines assessed to Young and Miller, Broughton’s punishment falls under the league’s rules governing hits on quarterbacks. The NFL reviews potential on-field violations after games, including plays that were not penalized by officials. Players also have the right to appeal fines under the league’s collectively bargained disciplinary procedures. item.title: Aday Mara experiences starstruck moment facing Nikola Jokic, Victor Wembanyama
item.description: The Oklahoma City Thunder have thrown Aday Mara into the deep end of the pool to start his NBA career. And the 7-foot-3 has calmly swum in the rocky waters. Since NBA training camp opened up earlier this month, Mara has completely rewritten his short-lived narratives. Not only has his conditioning improved tenfold, but he's helped the Thunder start off with an impressive 2-0 start in the 2026-27 regular season. In resume-strengthening wins over the San Antonio Spurs and Denver Nuggets , Mara held his own against two top-three NBA players in Victor Wembanyama and Nikola Jokic. Both had subpar games against OKC. The Thunder comfortably won both by double-digit points. Can't think of a tougher set of tests to start your NBA journey. Mara talked about being a little starstruck in both instances. In a basketball world where every big man wants to have guard-like handles, the 21-year-old is a blast from the past as he embraces his Godzilla-esque build. Remember, this is the same guy who listed all-time centers — Pau Gasol, Marc Gasol, Hakeem Olajuwon — as players he grew up idolizing. "Very crazy because last two games, it's been against Wembanyama and tonight was Jokic. Which is one of my favorite players — if not, my favorite player," Mara said. "I haven't think about it yet. But it's pretty crazy to play against those guys. I used to watch in the TV. But I think once I get in the court, I feel pretty comfortable." The Thunder are expecting big things from Mara both in the short-term and long-term future. He's helped from the jump. Something that was difficult to imagine after his sluggish Summer League outing. But he's completely transformed his conditioning over the last few months. Now, he's looking to be a ready-now contributor who could be a key piece in the long run. The Thunder look like they hit a home run with the No. 12 pick of the 2026 NBA draft. How It Happened 1st Quarter Tech started with two nothing runs by Justice Haynes before Alberto Mendoza hit Jordan Allen for 43 yards to keep the driv alive. Two plays later, Mendoza ran for 27 to put Tech with goal to go. From four yards out, Mendoza connected with Kevin Roche, Jr. in the back of the endzone to put the Jackets up 7-0. Tech only moved mere feet before a 3rd & 5 pass to Jordan Allen was left a yard short. Aidan Birr’s 20 yard field goal gave Tech the lead back into halftime at 13-12. 3rd Quarter Starting the half with the ball, BC rushed for 52 yards and easily scored on a two yard MacCormack touchdown rush. Opting to go for two, Mason McKenzie’s pass was broken up in the endzone, leaving BC’s lead at 18-13. Tech got good utilization from Tre Maddox on their next drive, driving the pile on a run and converting a first down on a quick screen pass to get to midfield. Mendoza on his next throw was intercepted after the ball bounced off Tech’s receiver and was caught by BC’s Charlie Comella. Facing 3rd & 11 on Tech’s next drive, Mendoza threw his second interception of the game, once again to Charlie Comella who returned it 53 yards for a pick six, extending BC’s lead to 42-20. Tech then brought in Grady Adamson at QB, where he completed five of six passes and finishing the drive with a 30 yard touchdown pass to Dalen Penson to make it 42-27. item.title: Former NBA player to plead guilty in federal sports betting case: Court filing
item.description: Former NBA player Malik Beasley intends to plead guilty to federal charges that accused him and five others of taking part in a bribery and betting scheme, according to a court notice filed overnight Saturday. Beasley, 29, had previously pleaded not guilty to four federal counts -- bribery in sporting contests, wire fraud conspiracy, honest services wire fraud conspiracy and money laundering conspiracy -- but the docket notice did not indicate what he would plead guilty to. The judge overseeing Beasley's case referred a "change of plea" to a federal magistrate in Brooklyn who will schedule a hearing at which Beasley will formally plead guilty. Heather Khalifa/AP Photo, FILE - PHOTO: In this July 1, 2026, file photo, former NBA player Malik Beasley, center, exits Brooklyn federal court in New York. Former NBA players Malik Beasley, Edward Davis indicted for alleged sports gambling scheme His attorney couldn't immediately be reached for comment. Beasley, who played for six different NBA teams over a nine-year career, allegedly agreed to underperform his statistics during the 2023-2024 season when he played for the Milwaukee Bucks so gamblers could win their bets, according to prosecutors. Gregory Shamus/Getty Images, FILE - PHOTO: In this April 24, 2025, file photo, Malik Beasley #5 of the Detroit Pistons shoots the ball during the first half against the New York Knicks in the Eastern Conference First Round NBA Playoffs at Little Caesars Arena in Detroit, Michigan. He had earned tens of millions of dollars during his career, but federal prosecutors accused Beasley of accumulating "multi-million dollar gambling losses" when he became part of the alleged scheme. NBA memo says league education needed about 'dire risks' of gambling The indictment mentioned four games in which Beasley would allegedly fix his performance while playing for the Bucks: against the Cleveland Cavaliers on Jan. 26, 2024; against the Charlotte Hornets on Feb. 27, 2024; against the Los Angeles Clippers on March 10, 2024; and against the Brooklyn Nets on March 21, 2024. Heather Khalifa/AP Photo, FILE - PHOTO: In this July 1, 2026, file photo, former NBA player Malik Beasley, center, exits Brooklyn federal court in New York. According to the indictment, Beasley's co-defendants allegedly selected games that would not be nationally televised and Beasley allegedly decided whether he would underperform or overperform his scoring and rebounding.

item.title: No. 13 Alabama pulls away in fourth quarter to deny Texas A&M's upset bid
item.description: Marcel Reed and Texas A&M overcame some early struggles but the Aggies' offense disappeared in the fourth quarter of Saturday's loss to Alabama. (Vasha Hunt/Associated Press) TUSCALOOSA, Ala. - Alabama scored two fourth-quarter touchdowns to hold off Texas A&M and secure a 31-20 victory Saturday, sending the Aggies into the off week with a 1-4 conference record. The Crimson Tide entered the fourth quarter down 20-17 but quarterback Keelon Russell threw two of his three touchdowns in the last frame while the Aggies' offense withered after the sun fell below the top deck of Bryant-Denny Stadium. It started when A&M quarterback Marcel Reed had his third turnover of the game, a fumbled snap on a fourth-and-1 play late in the third quarter that set up Alabama with a short field. Russell dropped a perfect pass to Rico Scott on third down and then found Marshall Pritchett for a touchdown on the first play of the fourth quarter to take the lead. After Texas A&M (4-4, 1-4 SEC) went three-and-out and punter Tyler White shanked a 29-yard punt to the Alabama 45, Russell led the Crimson Tide (6-2, 4-2) down the field in less than three minutes before finding Kaleb Edwards for another score to go up 31-20. Texas A&M cornerback Dezz Ricks (2) celebrates after his interception against Alabama during the first half of an NCAA college football game Saturday, Oct. 24, 2026, in Tuscaloosa, Ala. (AP Photo/Vasha Hunt) (Vasha Hunt/Associated Press) The Aggies were in the game despite Reed having his worst start of the season - and arguably of his career - as he threw two interceptions in the game's first five minutes. The first was a pick-six to Dijon Lee Jr., who jumped a hitch route and returned it 39 yards to the end zone. The second came on the next play from scrimmage, when Chuck McDonald III got his hands underneath a cross-field pass from Reed that got tipped on the way by an unblocked Red Morgan. But the Aggies lucked out when Conor Talty missed his first field goal of the season on the ensuing possession. Backup Brady Hart warmed up on the sideline after the second interception but Reed led the offense back out on the field, and instead of digging a further hole, the senior quarterback orchestrated back-to-back touchdown drives. Texas A&M went 80 yards on 10 plays on the first one and then 75 yards on 11 plays on the following drive. Reed was 7-for-8 passing for 104 yards and two total touchdowns, a 9-yard slant score to Mario Craver and a 4-yard keeper, on those two drives. When Reed scampered into end zone to finish off the second drive, it wasn't just that the Aggies were still in the game - they were winning 14-10. David Olano kicked a field goal on each side of halftime for the Aggies to go up 20-17 while Talty missed his second field goal of the game in the third quarter to give Texas A&M the advantage. Then came Reed's fumble. Alabama now leads the all-time series against Texas A&M 14-3. NO. 13 ALABAMA 31, TEXAS A&M 20 Texas A&M 7 10 3 0 - 20 Alabama 10

item.title: Minnesota Stuns No. 15 Iowa With Walk Off Field Goal
item.description: Photo by: Julia Hansen Gophers Deliver Dramatic Rivalry Victory The Minnesota Golden Gophers pulled off a dramatic rivalry victory on Saturday, defeating the No. 15 Iowa Hawkeyes 13-10 at Huntington Bank Stadium. Kicker Luke Drzewiecki delivered the decisive moment, connecting on a 46 yard field goal as time expired to give Minnesota the win and reclaim the Floyd of Rosedale trophy. The victory improved Minnesota to 5-2 overall and 3-1 in Big Ten play, providing a major boost after a disappointing 41-13 loss to Purdue in its previous game. Head coach P.J. Fleck’s team responded with a gritty defensive performance and made the necessary plays late to defeat its ranked rival. Defense Sets the Tone Offense was difficult to come by throughout the afternoon, with both teams struggling to sustain drives. Minnesota opened the scoring with a 31 yard field goal from Drzewiecki in the first quarter, but Iowa answered with a 32 yard kick from Caden Buhr in the second quarter to tie the game at 3-3. The Gophers finally broke through in the third quarter when running back Darius Taylor scored on a one-yard touchdown run. An Iowa offsides penalty helped keep the drive alive after the Hawkeyes initially appeared to stop Minnesota on fourth down. Minnesota’s defense played a crucial role, limiting Iowa’s normally productive rushing attack to just 90 yards. The Hawkeyes also committed four turnovers, including three interceptions, repeatedly giving away opportunities to take control of the game. Iowa Forces a Late Tie Despite Minnesota’s defensive dominance, Iowa found a way back into the contest during the fourth quarter. Quarterback Hank Brown connected with Reece Vander Zee for a 37 yard touchdown, completing a 98 yard scoring drive that tied the game at 10-10 with fewer than four minutes remaining. The Hawkeyes appeared to have momentum, but Minnesota answered with a clutch drive of its own. Quarterback Drake Lindsey connected with receiver Jalen Smith for a 39 yard completion on third down, moving the Gophers into position for the winning kick. Drzewiecki then calmly drilled the 46 yard field goal as the clock expired, sending the Minnesota crowd into celebration. Minnesota Builds Momentum The Gophers finished with just 209 total yards but did enough in key moments to secure the victory. The win also marked their first Floyd of Rosedale triumph since 2023. Minnesota now turns its attention toward another difficult matchup against No. 6 Indiana next weekend. After an emotional rivalry win, Fleck’s team will look to carry its defensive intensity into the next challenge.

item.title: Alpine issues statement after Jeremy Clarkson's controversial Franco Colapinto comments
item.description: Motorsport photo Alpine has released a statement in support of its driver Franco Colapinto after former Top Gear host Jeremy Clarkson joked on Sky Sports F1 that the driver had been given a grid penalty "for being Argentinian". Clarkson is spending the United States Grand Prix weekend with the Enstone outfit, which he has supported for several years as his local team, and he appeared on the live Sky Sports F1 broadcast at the Circuit of the Americas ahead of qualifying. The Clarkson's Farm presenter discussed several topics, including Colapinto's grid penalty, Martin Brundle's grid walk and Lewis Hamilton's partner, Kim Kardashian. "Franco’s got a grid penalty for being Argentinian. Probably. Well, I’d give him one for that," Clarkson joked when asked about Alpine's chances at the United States Grand Prix. "But anyway, that’s just because of what happened when we went there," he added, referencing one of the most controversial Top Gear episodes from when he, along with co-hosts James May and Richard Hammond, visited Patagonia in 2014. Franco Colapinto, Alpine Franco Colapinto, Alpine The trio fled the country when protests broke out and the crew was pelted with stones after Clarkson drove a Porsche 928 carrying the number plate H982 FKL, which locals believed was a reference to the 1982 Falklands War. Clarkson and the Top Gear crew have insisted the number plate was a coincidence and have denied it was chosen on purpose. Alpine released a statement following Clarkson's comments, backing Colapinto. "We at Alpine are aware of the comments made by a team guest in a recent television interview in Austin," the team said. "Franco is our driver and has our full support." While the statement does not name Clarkson, it closely followed the 66-year-old's comments. Colapinto was handed a 10-place grid penalty for this weekend's United States Grand Prix for receiving his fourth new control electronics unit of the 2026 season. item.title: George Russell calls for F1 rethink as cars are “forced to run so low and so stiff”
item.description: Motorsport photo Mercedes Formula 1 driver George Russell faces a challenging United States Grand Prix tomorrow as a disappointing qualifying means he'll start sixth. While his team-mate and championship leader Kimi Antonelli is starting on pole, the Briton argues that F1 may need to rethink how low and stiff the cars run following criticism of the bumps at the Circuit of the Americas. Red Bull's Max Verstappen was the first to raise complaints on Thursday ahead of the race weekend, with him describing the bumps as "unacceptable" and "out of control". Russell backed the Dutchman, but, following his poor Saturday, added that he believes the cars are just as much a part of the problem. “Yeah, I mean it is definitely pretty bad," he said on the track surface. "But it’s always a challenge when you’re forced to run the car so low and so stiff. If we can get it on the tracks, then maybe we need to think about how they allow us to run the cars in a more sensible region.” On Thursday, Russell called for F1 circuits to be resurfaced “every couple of years”, pointing out that the cars run just “10mm” from the ground at the end of the straight. COTA chairman Bobby Epstein has admitted the dip at Turn 1 is “not acceptable in my mind”, but told ESPN there is “no easy fix”. McLaren ’s Oscar Piastri compared it to “a motocross jump” after qualifying saw him finish seventh. George Russell, Mercedes George Russell, Mercedes The Mercedes driver's Saturday did not go to plan. He was 0.441 seconds off Antonelli, and said he simply failed to put a lap together in Q3. “I think from my side, it was two bad laps in Q3. Simple as that really, you know? item.title: Change captain? Play the kids? How to solve the problems at Manchester United
item.description: The beleaguered Michael Carrick’s job is on the line, but there are steps he can take to revive the stricken club The big question as Bournemouth arrive for Sunday’s 2pm kick-off at Old Trafford is whether Michael Carrick will show his authority by stripping the captaincy from Bruno Fernandes and/or dropping Manchester United’s five-times player of the year. On Friday, Carrick refused to deny he may do so, but the bigger picture concerns whether cashing in on the Portuguese and his fellow mutineer, Lisandro Martínez, in the winter window would be prescient to initiate a new era. Fernandes and Martínez are out of contract in the close season (the club has an extra year’s option in both cases) and, judging by recent behaviour, intend to leave. So yielding, say, £40m and £25m respectively for them in January would allow investment as the rebuild begins. Even a few days on, Fernandes’s words in Como seem incredible: “It’s a decision from the staff to not press man-to-man and sometimes leave space behind and try to get the ball, wait for them, but sometimes when you give space to these teams they get confidence,” he said after Wednesday’s 4-1 humiliation. Fernandes’s open questioning of the tactics is a challenge to the head coach’s authority and we wait to see how/if Carrick will face it down. If Carrick acts and proves he is not a lame duck then even if he is removed a favour is done for his successor. Continue reading...

item.title: Football Daily | Mourinho is ready for his clásico return – stock up on popcorn, folks!
item.description: Sign up now! Sign up now! Sign up now? Sign up now! Football Daily has never had much time for conspiracy theories. Lee Harvey Oswald dunnit, Stanley Kubrick didn’t fake the moon landing, Vinícius Jr doesn’t have a body double and Miranda isn’t a secret traitor. But our Spidey senses picked up when the UK government announced their Be Ready campaign on Thursday night. In case you missed it, or live outside the UK and couldn’t care less about this weird little island, we’ve lifted this from our news story : “Every Briton is being urged to stock up to nine litres of bottled water and three days’ worth of food in new government guidance designed to ensure that households can survive a weather, cyber or other serious emergency. The Be Ready campaign is aimed at persuading people to stock up with supplies to last 72 hours, amid growing official concern about the impact of the climate crisis, technological dependency and hostile state threats.” Would it not be much easier all round if the two big clubs in Manchester simply swapped all playing and coaching staff before the next round of fixtures? United would finally get the squad that Bruno Fernandes and Lisandro Martínez clearly feel they deserve, one of serial winners who are worthy of the club’s fine history (and free of the whiners). Meanwhile, City would might get a team that would make them (somewhat) competitive in the lower tiers where they’re surely headed. And a manager who has coached there quite recently. Sure there’d be a few grumbles from the fans, but more importantly in the current football climate, think of all the potential new shirt sales, and the Us-Against-the-World mentality that Enzo Maresca would be able to instil in his team whose own supporters would even hate them. And no-one would even have to move house. It’s a win-win solution. Although, no, it’s United; so probably a win-high-scoring-draw-against-Wycombe solution” – Justin Kavanagh. Like all right-minded people, I only read Big Website to get my fill of news and information (ahem …). However, I did come across a recent piece in The New Yorker on James Daunt, the chief suit of the US book chain Barnes & Noble (no relation). The billionaire Russian oligarch, Alexander Mamut, asked him 20 years ago how much it would cost to buy Waterstones, and when he was told it would be £40m, he looked pleased and just said, ‘That’s less than Fernando Torres’, before adding, ‘It’s not even half a boat’. Odd reference points these billionaires” – Noble Francis. May I be the first of 1,057 Daniels to say thank you for the good luck message at the end of Thursday’s Football Daily. It has put a little extra pep in my step today” – Daniel Mee. This is an extract from our daily football email … Football Daily. item.title: Is el clásico still the world’s biggest match? Three questions before Barcelona v Real Madrid
item.description: The fixture’s relevance waned as the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded. Can Lamine Yamal and Mbappé lift it into a new era? For the best part of a decade, el clásico was more than just soccer’s biggest fixture. It was the defining narrative. At the peak of the Lionel Messi v Cristiano Ronaldo era, there were clásicos everywhere. Yes, when the two historic rivals clashed on the pitch, but also in the voting for the Ballon d’Or every year and in so much of the discourse around the sport. As the Messi-Ronaldo rivalry faded, though, so too did the clásico ’s relevance. This isn’t to say matches between Barcelona and Real Madrid no longer matter. They always have and always will. item.title: Chaotic state of football in Brazil epitomises a nation where greed has conquered glory | Jonathan Liew
item.description: The national game merely reflects the mood in a divided nation which is going to the polls with very little faith in the power of democracy Look, cards on the table: I don’t know for certain, and nor do you, whether Flávio Bolsonaro – the man widely tipped to become the next president of Brazil after Sunday night’s election – really did steal an island from Richarlison. There are lawyers involved, claims and counter-claims, and in any case, adjudicating land ownership disputes between right-wing strongmen and Tottenham reserve-team strikers lies very much beyond this column’s spectrum of expertise. It’s why, for example, this newspaper took no official position on the well-publicised battle between Rodrigo Duterte and Vincent Janssen over that Polynesian isthmus. According to Richarlison, a few years ago he purchased an island off the southern coast of Rio de Janeiro, and has the documentation to prove it. Richarlison says Bolsonaro tried to buy it from him, and when he refused a lawyer named Willer Tomaz simply turned up and annexed it. “These guys took the island without spending a penny, as far as I know,” Richarlison claimed in an Instagram video that has been viewed more than 31 million times. Tomaz has accused Richarlison of lying, arguing that he has a public deed registered at the notary’s office. Bolsonaro, for his part, has denied any connection with the island in question and described Richarlison’s intervention as “politically motivated”. Continue reading...

item.title: Premier League: 10 things to look out for this weekend
item.description: Max Dowman may get a chance, Spurs need to find balance at Stamford Bridge and Axel Disasi must make amends Premier League top scorers After seven games, Nottingham Forest’s record is eerily similar to last season: five points, five goals scored. A year ago Forest’s eighth game was a 3-0 home loss to Chelsea that marked the end for Ange Postecoglou , the second of four managers to occupy the dugout last term. There is no suggestion that Oliver Glasner is under similar scrutiny yet, but the Austrian needs to find solutions for the league’s lowest scorers. Morgan Gibbs-White is available after missing the narrow defeat by Arsenal , while Liam Delap may benefit from a return to familiar surroundings – 12 of his 14 career Premier League goals were scored for Ipswich, six of them at Portman Road. “What we need to improve is getting [Delap] into more positions where he can score,” Glasner said before Friday evening’s game. “He’s one of our best finishers.” Gary O’Neil also lacks a standout scorer, but he is squeezing goals out of his side. Eight different Ipswich players have scored in seven games; only Brighton and Brentford can better that total this season. item.title: Manchester City have been a joy to watch but they became detached from their roots | Philipp Lahm
item.description: City behaved much like other top clubs but their rule-breaking deserves to be punished. The Bundesliga, where members have a controlling stake, can show the way forward Do we have to reassess Manchester City now? In my columns, I have repeatedly engaged with this club and its key figures. Looking back at what I have written over the years, I believe it remains beyond question that the team have achieved greatness. I always loved watching them: they were a true unit on the pitch, a finely tuned orchestra. I would also write all over again that the conductor, Pep Guardiola, masters his craft like few others. I could recognise his teams even if they were wearing the wrong shirts and the game was broadcast in black and white – by the passes, the distances between the players and the intelligence of their interplay. It is no wonder Guardiola inspires others to become managers; look at Vincent Kompany, Mikel Arteta, Enzo Maresca, and perhaps some time Ilkay Gündogan and Rodri. Continue reading...

item.title: Will that do? Lamine Yamal conjures another magical spell as Barça pass first test | Sid Lowe
item.description: The 19-year-old scored a cracker in Seville, days after his ‘almost rabona’ at Galatasaray, as La Liga leaders beat Real Betis When at last it was time for Lamine Yamal to leave, the 19-year-old’s number going up before the 90th minute for only the second time since the opening day, Real Betis fans whistled him all the way to the touchline where Barcelona’s coach was waiting. His work here was done, Hansi Flick invited him to take the weight off his feet and his shoulders, not that he wanted to. First, though, he took Lamine Yamal’s head in his hands and, leaning in away from the amateur lip readers, tried to make himself heard over the noise. “I told him I was proud of him because he played a fantastic game,” he said. At least he could think of something. When Lamine Yamal had opened the scoring just nine minutes into the match that was supposed to find out how good Barcelona really were, it hadn’t been easy. Nothing erudite, anyway. On the morning that Barcelona went to Betis – first v third, a proper opponent at last – Jorge Valdano had lamented that sometimes he doesn’t have the words, and he always has the words. Valdano had just watched Lamine do that , whatever that was , in Istanbul – an “almost rabona ”, the kid called it – and now he had a problem. “If he keeps doing strange things, we’re not going to be able to explain it,” he wrote . item.title: Brighton are the apex B club – their next target should be a Champions League place | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: Diego Gómez’s wondergoal in a five-star demolition is just the latest in an impressive run of results for the south coast team Sign up for our free newsletter here For two or three years now, it’s been standard to nod approvingly at how well-run Brighton, Brentford and Bournemouth are, and to move on. What else is there to say? It’s true, of course – these are sides who have made the most of relatively limited resources. But there’s also an underlying assumption in the designation: that these are clubs who have no higher aspiration, that their limit is earning praise for upper mid-table finishes. This season, perhaps, offers an opportunity to change that. Other than Arsenal, every major club is undergoing significant transition. Manchester City may have started the season with seven straight wins, but there’s every chance the punishment for their multiple breaches of Premier League regulations takes them out of the race for the top five. In that context, why shouldn’t one of those efficient smaller sides qualify for the Champions League? Continue reading...

item.description: Another round of games and another disappointing draw for Arsenal while Manchester City sit top of the table with a 100% record There would have been hope that the international break could offer the Arsenal players and staff a reset but the same problems reared their head at the Emirates on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Birmingham. As they have done so often this season, the Gunners dominated most attacking and possession-based metrics – they registered 76% possession, a 2.73 xG and 43 touches in the opposition box – but their profligacy in front of goal and lack of urgency in their play once again came to the fore. Of their 27 chances, they managed just four on target as they toiled against a resilient opposition who understood the playbook. Birmingham set up in a strong defensive structure, protecting their box admirably with numbers to frustrate Renée Slegers’s side, who famously struggle to break down low blocks. item.title: Europe is a blast – but more a curse than a blessing if you are not a Premier League super-club I Jonathan Wilson
item.description: The four Premier League clubs playing in the lesser continental competitions face each other on Sunday – but three are struggling domestically The sun shone. The temperature was in the high 20s. There was a mood of great conviviality. If you were struggling with the official allocation, it turned out you could just email the president of Torreense and he’d sort you out. Were these “Nuno-tickets” real? It turned out they were. Not only that, but you could sit anywhere you wanted in a stadium too big for the game and, if you happened to have gravitated to the comfortable hospitality seating at the back of the lower tier, the beer was inexplicably free. Locals in Leiria seemed bewildered but could hardly have been more accommodating. A beer pump had been installed outside a patisserie on the Praça Francisco Rodrigues Lobo, whose owner soon found fans happy to help stack empty barrels if that facilitated the free flow of Sagres. “There was a meeting at the town hall to explain these are not hooligans,” said the owner of a radical leftist flammkuchen restaurant between the square and the cathedral. “They told us the club comes from the labour movement and I found that very interesting.” And how had she found the fans? “Noisy, but with a quirky sense of humour.” Continue reading...

item.title: James McClean: ‘Wearing the poppy was just never going to happen’
item.description: The former Republic of Ireland international on growing up in a community still reeling from the Troubles and the controversy that scarred his career “The perception of me is that, basically, I am a madman,” James McClean says calmly. “I’m outspoken. I’m a loudmouth. I’m very opinionated and I hate all things British. That’s from people who don’t know me. The reality is quite the opposite. I’m pretty boring. I go training, go home and switch off. A lot of my days are quite bland, quite basic.” McClean sounds as sane as he looks gaunt on a bleak Monday in Derry. He spent 14 years in English football and the fact that he is now at war with his own club, Derry City, can’t obscure the fact that he is the fifth-most-capped Republic of Ireland international, having played 103 times. “People define success in different ways,” he says, “but I’m the only footballer from the north of Ireland to win over 100 caps for Ireland. I played 150 Premier League games over five seasons, 800 professional games and won a lot of individual accolades. I count that as success and don’t look back with regrets.” Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17. Written mainly by Júlia Belas Trindade and Sophie Downey , expect guest appearances from stars such as Anita Asante, Ada Hegerberg and many more. Try our other sports emails: as well as the occasionally funny football email The Fiver from Monday to Friday, there are weekly catch-ups for cricket in The Spin and rugby union in The Breakdown , and our seven-day roundup of the best of our sports journalism in The Recap .
